sources.name: BookMyShow

reviews.summary: Sacnilk revised overseas receipts for 16–20 November. The five daily changes add ₹24.00 crore to the worldwide run. The dated report agrees with the revised series. US and Canadian receipts still include a provisional $500,000 for Friday.
reviews.next: Recheck the 20 November North American estimate and the 21 November full-day gross. Sacnilk lists ₹33.05 crore in India and ₹53.05 crore worldwide on Saturday. The Numbers stops on Friday, Mojo’s Saturday chart was empty, and Boxoffy’s count was partial.

reviews.summary: Friday 20 November remains the common cutoff. The Numbers and Box Office Mojo list $500,000 for Friday in the US and Canada. Boxoffy estimates about $830,000 for Saturday from 52,448 counted tickets. The new weekend tables show each publisher’s theater count and gross per theater.
reviews.next: Check The Numbers and Box Office Mojo for a full-day US and Canadian gross and cumulative total for 21 November, and for confirmation of Friday’s estimate. Sacnilk reports ₹33.05 crore in India and ₹53.05 crore worldwide on Saturday, taking its cumulative totals to ₹1,084.00 crore and ₹1,651.00 crore.

reviews.summary: Edition 3 adds six weekly market charts, figures for 24 other markets, two release watchlists and reception from five additional markets. Reporting periods vary by market. The daily series retains the reconciled R-002 totals through 20 November.
reviews.next: Check the next international charts as their publishers release them, including the first local grosses for Brazil and Mexico. Revisit the 20 November US/Canada estimate and the full-day 21 November report before extending the daily charts.

reviews.summary: The third weekend added ₹137.35 crore worldwide and ₹94.35 crore in India on Sacnilk’s gross series. The Numbers estimates $2.171 million in the US and Canada. Four revised worldwide entries reduce the earlier 20 November total by ₹15 crore.

sourceNotes.text: The Numbers revised Friday to $494,000. Its three provisional daily entries bring the series to $28,514,872, which rounds to its published $28,515,000. Mojo’s complete daily rows add to $2,065,000 for the weekend and $28,408,872 through Sunday. Its weekend page showed a Friday–Saturday subtotal at review time.

Sacnilk’s revised daily rows sum to the dated Sunday worldwide total of ₹1,689.50 crore. Bollywood Hungama maintains its own India series. Its India net and Sacnilk’s tax-inclusive India gross measure different receipts.

Two additions fill gaps in the existing sources. The Cinetel chart on ComingSoon.it extends Italian coverage beyond opening day. Comscore’s estimates, as reported by Bollywood Hungama, supply a worldwide weekend rank in US dollars across 64 territories.

reviews.next: Recheck US/Canada weekend actuals against the daily and weekend reports. Read the next Dutch and Nigerian film-level charts and the New Zealand local-currency report. Revisit Brazil’s ANCINE data and Mexico’s CANACINE chart for their first verified local grosses.

opportunities.title: North American theater counts
opportunities.next: Both weekend grosses match the daily ledger. For 13–15 November, The Numbers reports 1,110 theaters and Box Office Mojo reports 1,112. Keep both attributions when revisiting these weekends.

opportunities.title: UK weekend performance
opportunities.next: Read the next weekend workbook and its preview footnotes. Preserve the £1 difference between the two publishers in the 13–15 November reports.

opportunities.title: India admissions and language mix
opportunities.next: Check dated reports for two complete periods. Record footfalls and language-level net in separate series, reconciling the language sum to all-India net within rounding.

opportunities.title: Effect of the exchange rate
opportunities.next: Match two reported gross dates to available H.10 observations and document the holiday rule before showing a dated-rate comparison.

items.text: Comscore estimated $13.765 million across 64 territories for the weekend, behind The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping and Ebenezer.
TheWrap reported that Ramayana had overtaken Dhurandhar: The Revenge. Sacnilk put the earlier film at $28.64 million, still above both Sunday estimates for Ramayana.
Ramayana opened the Films from BRICS programme at the 57th International Film Festival of India in Panaji.
Eagle Pictures’ release earned €85,872 on 113 screens over four days, placing 16th in Italy.
Saturday took Sacnilk’s all-language India net to ₹907.15 crore. Its Sunday report put the weekend at ₹79.00 crore net.
